title: Epistle participles and infinitives
subtitle: Attach non-finite forms to a claim, not to thin air.
overview: In epistles, participles and infinitives often expand an assertion, express purpose, or turn an action into a noun-like phrase.
Ask what governs the form and what it contributes: description, circumstance, content, purpose, or result.

sections.title: Attachment questions
rows: what purpose or result is named?

items.grc: ἵνα δῷ ὑμῖν ... κραταιωθῆναι διὰ τοῦ πνεύματος.
items.en: So that he may grant you ... to be strengthened through the Spirit.
For you to walk worthily of God; identify its governing expression in context.
